subject: Urgent: Pegasus production 503/latency spike — suspected peering/DNS handoff
messages:
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@pegasus-retail.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <ops+infra@pegasus-retail.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production 503 spike — multiple customers, started 09:07 UTC

Hi Logan,

We started seeing a large spike in 503s and tail latency across user-facing inference endpoints at ~09:07 UTC. Error rate jumped from <0.1% to ~6% and p95 latency spiked from ~120ms to >2.5s. Impacting checkout flows for several large merchants.

Observed: 
- Consistent 503/504 from routes routed via us-east-1 peering path.
- Sample request IDs: 3c9a-...-b7e2, 8d11-...-f4c3 (attached logs).
- Our ops team saw long DNS resolution times (8–12s) to model.service.redwood.com around the same window.

We pulled a proxy trace (attached) and traceroutes show packet handovers that look like repeated NAT retries between peers. Can your team confirm if there's an ongoing VPC peering or firewall change? This is S1 for us.

Tom
Tom Alvarez
VP Engineering, Pegasus Retail

Attachments: proxy_trace_20271130.zip
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@pegasus-retail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Production 503 spike — suspected peering/DNS handoff

Tom — thanks for the data, and sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as P0. Initial read: symptoms look like a combination of (a) intermittent VPC peering path flapping and (b) DNS failover/long TTLs causing client retries to hit congested NAT/proxy appliances.

Immediate actions we are running now:
- Vivek and infra running targeted traceroutes + NAT table checks on the peering path.
- Temporarily routing Pegasus traffic to our secondary peering link in us-west-2 (expected <10m to switch).
- Increasing firewall NAT ephemeral table size to reduce ephemeral exhaustion risk.
- Monica: preparing a customer-facing status update and asking Pegasus to hold off on any batch jobs.

Can you confirm you can pause the analytics batch window? Also sharing short mitigation plan below.

Mitigation plan (short):
1) Divert Pegasus traffic to standby peering (us-west-2).
2) Increase NAT table & bypass heavyweight inspection for pegged subnets for 30m.
3) Force DNS TTL refresh for model.service.redwood.com via our authoritative cache (invalidate).
4) After stabilization, capture full NAT metrics and do a deeper postmortem.

I will update in 15m with traceroute and NAT status.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Senior TAM, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Production 503 spike — suspected peering/DNS handoff

Logan — quick findings from infra:

- Traceroutes (attached) show repeated asymmetric hops between our us-east-1 egress and Pegasus' ingress; we see 4–8x retransmissions at the peering NAT.
- NAT ephemeral table at the edge peaked at 98% of configured capacity between 09:03–09:09 UTC; there were ~2.1k retries/sec.
- DNS: our authoritative resolver did a failover to the secondary nameserver at 09:06:18 UTC; secondary had an outdated zone (old A records) resulting in clients holding stale entries and repeatedly reconnecting.

Immediate technical recommendations executed: 
- Increased NAT ephemeral table from 65k -> 120k entries (live change).
- Pushed an authoritative cache purge for model.service.redwood.com across our edge resolvers (propagation ~30s).
- Applied a temporary bypass rule for payload inspection for Pegasus /32 ranges while we observe.

Next: capture complete NAT logs and a timeline for TTL propagation. I attached traceroutes_pegasus_1105.txt.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: traceroutes_pegasus_1105.txt
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@pegasus-retail.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T10:28:00Z
Subject: Update: Pegasus — mitigation in progress

Tom — quick customer update from Redwood: 

Sorry for the disruption this morning. We're actively mitigating a peering/NAT exhaustion issue that temporarily caused DNS and proxy failovers. Our SREs have increased NAT capacity, purged the authoritative cache, and are routing traffic to a secondary peering link while we validate stability. Expected time to full recovery: 20–40 minutes.

Request for Pegasus: if you can pause the analytics batch jobs that kick off hourly, that will reduce load on your egress and help confirm steady state sooner. Will follow up once we see sustained p95 <250ms and error rate <0.5%.

Thank you for your patience — we know this hits checkout and revenue flows, and we have prioritized containment.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

--
On Tue, Nov 30, 2027 at 09:40 Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Tom — thanks for the data, and sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as P0....
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@pegasus-retail.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T10:45:12Z
Subject: Re: Update: Pegasus — mitigation in progress

Monica — confirmed, we paused the analytics batch window at 10:25 UTC. We're seeing error rate drop from 6% -> 0.4% and p95 back to ~180–220ms in the last 10 minutes. Thank you.

I'll hold on any further changes, please let me know when you're ready for a full postmortem.

Tom
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T16:02:00Z
Subject: Pegasus incident — exec summary & ask for credits/next steps

Team — concise executive summary for leadership/finance: 

What happened: a combination of peering path instability and an authoritative DNS failover to a stale secondary nameserver caused client reconnection storms and near-exhaustion of NAT ephemeral tables on the us-east-1 egress path. This produced elevated 503s and high p95 latency for Pegasus between ~09:03–10:20 UTC.

Impact: 
- Pegasus saw peak error rate ~6% and p95 latency >2.5s; checkout impact for multiple merchants; they paused analytics jobs to remediate.
- Customer severity: S1; they escalated to VP Eng (Tom Alvarez).
- No data exfiltration reported.

What we did: 
- Increased NAT ephemeral capacity, purged authoritative cache, routed traffic to standby peering, and applied temporary inspection bypass for impacted prefixes.
- Customer-facing communications sent; customer paused batch jobs which aided recovery.

Ask: 
- Please approve a one-time service credit (pro-rata for outage window) and a follow-up Deep Dive (postmortem) including: root cause across peering config, DNS zone management hygiene, and NAT sizing guidelines.
- Owner for postmortem: Vivek to lead tech write-up; Monica to lead customer RCA and comms; Logan to coordinate timeline.

I'll circulate a draft postmortem by EOD tomorrow and propose remediation steps (automated NAT scaling, DNS secondary health checks, and canary peering failover tests).

—Logan
Logan Wright
Senior TAM, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: proxy_trace_20271130.zip, traceroutes_pegasus_1105.txt
